narrative.h2: Country MVs run on trucks, fields, and neon bar light

sections.heading: What country looks like
sections.body: Country music video has a well-defined visual canon that the genre's audience expects and rewards. The signatures: pickup trucks (Ford F-150 and Chevy Silverado, dust-covered), golden-hour wheat or cornfields, weathered cowboy hats and pearl-snap shirts, dive-bar interiors with neon beer signs as key light, front-porch shots, dirt roads receding into hills. Color grade is warm and slightly desaturated, with a hint of teal in shadows. Handheld is acceptable; drone shots over fields are mandatory.

sections.heading: Reference points that actually work
sections.body: The references span eras: Luke Combs' 'Beautiful Crazy', Morgan Wallen's 'Whiskey Glasses', Kacey Musgraves' 'Slow Burn' and 'Rainbow' (the modern, art-directed end), Chris Stapleton's 'Tennessee Whiskey' CMA live performance, Carrie Underwood's 'Before He Cheats', and Zach Bryan's intentionally lo-fi clips. Directors Trey Fanjoy (Taylor Swift's 'Tim McGraw', Carrie Underwood), Wes Edwards (Luke Combs, Brad Paisley), Justin Clough, and Roman White shape much of the contemporary look. Tunee's country model knows the difference between bro-country bright and Americana muted.

sections.heading: Prompting tip for Tunee
sections.body: Specify the sub-genre — bro-country (party-bright, neon bar, lifted truck), Americana (muted, porch, vintage Wrangler), or modern-pop country (Nashville rooftop, fashion-forward). A prompt naming the truck make, the bar's beer-sign brand, or the field crop produces a sharper frame than 'country music scene'. Audiences notice when the props are wrong.
